<section id="A7.SS6.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">G.6.1 </span>t-test: MIRA vs. LLM4Teach</h4>

<div id="A7.SS6.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS6.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To assess whether the performance differences between LLM4Teach and MIRA are statistically significant, we conduct Welch’s t-tests on the evaluation metrics across environments and seeds. Welch’s t-test is a two-sample statistical test that does not assume equal variance. As shown in Table <a href="#A7.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ G.6 MiniGrid Performance Summary ‣ Appendix G Extended Experimental Studies ‣ MIRA: Memory-Integrated Reinforcement Learning Agent with Limited LLM Guidance" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, none of the differences reach significance at the <math id="A7.SS6.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> level. This suggests that MIRA performs comparably to LLM4Teach across all reported metrics, despite MIRA having small lower final reward.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While MIRA improves sample efficiency and reduces reliance on frequent LLM queries, it also comes with natural trade-offs. The method relies on offline LLM outputs to initialize its memory graph, which, if they include misleading information or are not well aligned with the environment dynamics, can slow convergence or increase the need for online queries. Our screening and pruning mechanisms reduce this risk, and in practice it is largely a limitation of current LLMs that is expected to diminish as models improve. MIRA also introduces shaping terms that require hyperparameter tuning to avoid instability between the actor and critic. We find, however, that they can be adjusted with standard procedures. Finally, our current study focuses on discrete action spaces; extending MIRA to continuous domains without discretization is a natural next step.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Reproducibility</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Experiments were run on both a Linux server with Intel Xeon E5-2630 v4 CPUs (40 threads) and an Apple M2 (8-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB unified memory). All LLM models used in our experiments correspond to the publicly available versions released in the first week of August 2025.</p>
</div>
<section id="A9.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.1 </span>Simulation Platforms</h3>

<section id="A9.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">I.1.1 </span>Gymnasium Toy text</h4>

<div id="A9.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Environment Details.</span>
Horizon indicates the maximum number of steps per episode before automatic termination (i.e., maxsteps in the environment configuration).</p>
</div>

<div id="A9.SS1.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS1.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Observation Space</span> In MiniGrid environments, the agent receives an RGB image of the grid, which is passed through a convolutional encoder <a href="#A9.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ I.1.2 Minigrid and BabyAI ‣ I.1 Simulation Platforms ‣ Appendix I Reproducibility ‣ MIRA: Memory-Integrated Reinforcement Learning Agent with Limited LLM Guidance" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> to extract spatial features relevant for navigation and interaction.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A9.F18" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17930v1/figs/cnn.png" id="A9.F18.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:384/155;" width="384" height="155" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 18: </span>Convolutional encoder architecture used to process the agent’s <math id="A9.F18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="56\times 56\times 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>56</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>56</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">56\times 56\times 3</annotation></semantics></math> RGB observation in MiniGrid environments. The input passes through a series of Conv2D layers, reducing spatial dimensions while increasing channel depth. The final activation is flattened and fed to both policy and value heads. This encoder captures spatial layout, object presence, and agent-centric context for decision-making.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A9.SS1.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS1.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This CNN processes the visual input into a compact feature vector, capturing object positions, colors, and layout structure.
The resulting embedding is concatenated with a learned directional encoding and passed to the policy and value heads for action selection and value estimation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.2 </span>LLM Confidence Settings</h3>

<div id="A9.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For completions where token-level likelihoods are available, confidence is computed using an exponential of the geometric-mean log-probability (<math id="A9.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\exp\left({1}/{L}\sum\log p_{i}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>∑</mo><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\exp\left({1}/{L}\sum\log p_{i}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>) with a fixed likelihood threshold of <math id="A9.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\geq 0.65" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.65</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\geq 0.65</annotation></semantics></math>. When likelihoods are unavailable, we obtain k independent completions (<math id="A9.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=3</annotation></semantics></math>) and retain only outputs that pass a majority-consistency test with a fixed agreement threshold <math id="A9.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\geq 2/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\geq 2/3</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="Ax2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Use of Large Language Models (LLMs)</h2>

<div id="Ax2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During the preparation of this manuscript, the authors used OpenAI’s ChatGPT to assist with grammar and readability. No research ideas, technical content, or analysis were generated by the tool. All content was reviewed and verified by the authors, who take full responsibility for the final version.</p>
</div>
</section>
